title: Machine learning picks AgCuTi wetting conditions on WCu that experiments confirm
summary: Eight regression models were trained on 125 full-factorial wetting experiments varying temperature, titanium content and surface roughness; the best, a support vector regressor (held-out R2 0.945), screened 37,572 candidate conditions and selected 10 representative ones. Experiments at those conditions matched predicted contact angles with a mean absolute error of 0.55 degrees (R2 0.91). A second gradient-boosting model with SHAP attributed about 70% of the contribution to the three process variables, with post-wetting morphology adding correlational information. This is a non-peer-reviewed preprint from a single laboratory and a narrow design space.
ai_technology: Support vector regression and gradient boosting models with SHAP interpretation of brazing-alloy wetting experiments.
organization: North China University of Water Resources and Electric Power

evidence.tested: 10 model-selected process conditions run experimentally; measured contact angles compared with predictions.
evidence.unknown: Whether the selected conditions improve joint performance, reproducibility in other labs, extrapolation beyond the sampled ranges; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: The trained regression model screened the process space and chose the conditions that were tested.

source_review.scope: Independent review: abstract from Europe PMC, Crossref posting date, OpenAlex title search. Full text not read.
